During her tenure as Florida Attorney General, Sen. Ashley Moody led an
investigation into the work-release program that allowed Jeffrey Epstein to
engage in sexual encounters while imprisoned for soliciting underage girls for
prostitution. After nearly two years of probing, she concluded no wrongdoing.
Now Moody, a Republican, is up for reelection in a tight race for a Florida
Senate seat against Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon, and she has received
$50,000 from individuals connected to Epstein.

Douglas Band, a former Bill Clinton staffer who communicated with Ghislaine
Maxwell to schedule meetings between the former president and Jeffrey Epstein,
donated $14,000 to Moody's victory fund on April 15. Blackstone CEO Stephen
Schwarzman and John Catsimatidis, two billionaires who appeared respectively
in call logs and address books in the Epstein files, donated the next most to
Moody's fund at $12,000 and $10,000 a pop. Apollo Global Management CEO Marc
Rowan, another billionaire who maintained a relationship with Epstein even
after the disgraced financier had been jailed for solicitation of prostitution
from a minor, and Ronald Lauder, the billionaire heir to the Estee Lauder
companies who appeared in the Epstein files for meetings and joint purchasing
agreements with Epstein, both chipped in $7,000.

Moody announced her probe on August 6, 2019, four days before Epstein's death
and shortly after Gov. Ron DeSantis ordered the transfer of an internal
investigation being conducted by Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw to the
Florida Department Of Law Enforcement. Two days later on August 8, Moody
immediately found that the work release had not been authorized by a judge.
("We have not been able to locate any administrative order, nothing in the
transcript, that would indicate that the judge was aware of ordered work
release in this particular case," she told local media.) Yet it took almost
two years for her office to finish investigating how law enforcement allowed
Epstein's work release to go forward.

NBC News has [since substantiated claims](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-
news/epstein-florida-jail-women-exploitation-work-release-palm-beach-
rcna347186) that Epstein abused the Palm Beach work-release program, which
allowed eligible inmates to leave detention for up to 16 hours a day, multiple
days a week, to resume working their jobs or completing approved projects.
They reported in June 2026 that, "At least five women say they had sexual
encounters with Epstein while he was participating in the jail's now-defunct
work-release program, according to records released this year by the Justice
Department as part of the agency's Epstein investigation. The encounters
occurred at his office in West Palm Beach and in a car parked outside the
county jail, the women said in FBI interviews."

Nevertheless, Moody's FDLE investigation wrapped up in May 2021, concluding no
noticeable misconduct by the sheriff's office or state prosecutors in Palm
Beach County in granting Epstein said work release. Upon the conclusion of the
investigation, former FBI agent Stuart Kaplan criticized its lack of search
warrants, subpoenas, or a grand jury. "It appears the FDLE solely depended
upon the cooperation and memory of those involved," Kaplan [told West Palm
Beach TV](https://www.wptv.com/news/epstein/fdle-investigation-finds-no-
wrongdoing-by-pbso-state-attorneys-office-in-jeffrey-epstein-plea-deal).

Sarah Kellen, a former aide to Epstein, testified before the House Oversight
Committee that Epstein paid Palm Beach County law enforcement officers for
preferential treatment, though she did not specify how much.

Ashley Moody's campaign did not respond to a request for comment.

Florida's U.S. Senate race has only recently come into play electorally as
President Donald Trump's abysmal approval ratings have dragged downballot GOP
candidates underwater across the country. Amid his unpopular war in Iran, the
president has seen his favorability in the sunshine state [shift
from](https://civiqs.com/results/approve_president_trump_2025?uncertainty=true&zoomIn=true&annotations=true&map=true)
+9 at the start of his second term to -14 with three weeks until election day,
according to Civiqs.

Meanwhile, Nixon, an insurgent now endorsed by Sens. Bernie Sanders and
Elizabeth Warren, overcame a roughly 17:1 fundraising disadvantage in the
Democratic primary to upset the establishment's pick, Alex Vindman, on August
18. Since then, [polls have
shown](https://floridapolitics.com/archives/823921-new-st-pete-polls-survey-
has-ashley-moody-at-47-angie-nixon-at-45-and-the-senate-race-still-inside-the-
margin-of-error/) Nixon closing within as few as 2 percentage points of Moody.

Sanders recently announced four joint Fighting Oligarchy campaign events set
to take place with Nixon on October 17 and 18 in Tampa, Melbourne,
Gainesville, and Tallahassee. An ascendant national figure, Nixon has
campaigned on a bold progressive agenda that includes Medicare for All, a
federal jobs guarantee with inflation adjusted wages, universal childcare, and
a national rent freeze and moratorium on evictions.

Moody, on the other hand, cast the deciding vote in July 2025 to table an NDAA
amendment that would have directed the Attorney General to "make publicly
available documents related to Jeffrey Epstein," and has at every turn
defended the Trump administration's illegal war in Iran, voting 12 times
against War Powers Resolutions.

Fast forward one year to July 2026, Moody positioned herself as a key defender
of Attorney General Todd Blanche, a key architect of the Epstein files
coverup, during his confirmation hearing to succeed Pam Bondi at the DOJ.
While Democrats highlighted his role in burying the files and past as Trump's
personal attorney, Moody listed awards Blanche received while he "prosecuted
drug traffickers and violent criminals" as a prosecutor in the Southern
District of New York.

Trump has returned the favor for her loyalty,
[offering](https://x.com/realDonaldTrump/status/2101031823622934637?s=20)
Moody his "Complete and Total Endorsement" and saying the passage of the Big
Beautiful Bill "probably wouldn't have happened" without her. Moody [accepted
Trump's
endorsement](https://x.com/ashleymoodyfl/status/1948548827621064912?s=42) in
stride, saying she's "incredibly honored" to have his support.
